```md
# Steering-lite BS-bench rewrite

Rewrite the benchmark from vjp-steering on the existing branch. Make a cheap first comparison of steering strength and precision on sycophancy, suitable for use and demo.

## User-visible result
On `rewrite/bsbench-vjp`, a clean cached Modal `just sweep` will compare steering-lite methods, VJP-cache and VJP-diff with prompting/random/mean-difference/PCA controls on 20 numbered Qwen3.5-4B BS-bench v2 questions, validate persona pairs, save on/off-target scores and blind change descriptions, produce matching reference-style HTML/PNG plots and maximum-coherent/optimal-dose tables, and test cheap method/model-specific RMS-KL calibration on about four new-data cases, for less than $50.

## Preferences and authority
- Initial GPU runs and judge calls together cost <$50; use cheaper workers, not Astra. Terra and DeepSeek V4 Flash are approved; keep one implementation writer at a time.
- Preserve the existing judge protocol; add a separate blind call. Dose-selection score: directed intended effect − 4 × off-target effect; retain the full Pareto frontier.
- This is experimental development, not a publication-proof study. No public posting or larger-model spending without separate approval.

## User voice
> can we add VJP-cache and VJP-diff

> yes please. also I wonder if we should uplift steering-lite to match vjp-steering so
>
> - **pairs** I would bring in minimal things in a clean way from  https://github.com/wassname/persona-steering-template-library, namely consider judge validation of the prefix and suffix? and perhaps it can be the same judge and reused from the eval? ok that's the steering personas
>   - but I would also like to use the judge (slow) or activation or J lens to validate if the person pairs correspond to the intended  
> - **calibration** I'm searching for a good way to calibrate so I can find the best dose cheaply and compare pareto optimal or max doses. A grid search is the most expensive. An iteratitive search such as an method of successive approximation (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iterative_method) is faster. But I'v found that (https://github.com/wassname/isokl_steering_calibration). I hope It can find the hyperparameter "target rmse(KL) [nats]" once per method/model, and it will allow quick calibration from then on. I would like to prove this... showing it predict's the max coherent dose on other datasets. (in any case it's better than what other papers and libraries do which is: no think about or talk about this at all, or do a super expensive grid search which I just can't afford).
> - **eval: faithfull** I found using a judge it usefull when the eval is not fully aligned with the steering, the judge can tell use "the effect is bluntness" but we aimed for honesty. another steering method might be more faithful. In fact the eval I used in jvp-steering seems good: it's fairly cheap (100 generations), fairly sensitive, has a nice graph showing the parto, and people understand sycophancy.
> - **platform** run on modal for speed, and still at low cost, and able to scale up from the initial Qwen 3.5 4B model to ~30B or 100+B
>
> so in the end I hope to redo steering-lite with a bullshit bench v2, judged eval, and my nice plot. Hopefully I can have a max dose and optimal dose table too. And compare to prompting as a baseline. Keeping the random zone, and mean mass diff, and PCA baseline.
>
> I migth use the 20 q dev versions first. ofc  the eval needs to be numbered. 
> In the end I hope to show the best steering method, ansering these questions
>
> which is the best (powerful and precise)?
> is it reliable? does it steer the concept we want fiathfully? does it scale to larger models? and I want a) html plot like vjp-steering (you need to view both png's and compare parity), b) corresponding max dose, and pareto optimal table
>
> the judge must also (this is a bew feature) 1) guess the concept being steered (ideally blind) this will tell us how faithfull it in
>
> need to be clean. we need to be able to run on modal with a `just sweep` where previuslly run ones are cached. we need to use https://github.com/wassname/vjp-steering as a base

> use cheaper models for subagents not astra

## Goals
1. [ ] goal: Rewrite the BS-bench v2 benchmark and compare VJP-cache/VJP-diff with the controls
   - Scope: reuse vjp-steering, preserve steering-lite variants including cache Gram, and include bare, prompting, random, mean difference and PCA; implement cache-value VJPs and reuse VJP-delta as VJP-diff, not a duplicate method.
   - Subtle failure mode: a parallel framework or a nonzero but wrong gradient looks like the requested rewrite.
   - Discriminator: the branch runs the real numbered benchmark; tiny-model extraction, actual cache-value derivatives, attachment, generation and save/load agree with independent checks, including Qwen3.5 hybrid attention.
   - Evidence:
     - Phase-1 cache-value derivatives: commits `2a5ddd3`, `269becf`, `56d10ed`; independent Qwen3.5 hybrid pipeline rerun `48 passed in 46.69s`.
     - Phase-2 local benchmark integration: commit `f26b001`; exact vjp-steering 100-row cohort with fixed numbered first 20, all eight conditions through train/save-load/attach/generate, cache invalidation and ledger tests. Worker full suite: `66 passed in 288.38s`; supervisor focused rerun: `11 passed in 149.83s`.
2. [ ] goal: Validate persona pairs and report judged effects plus blind change descriptions
   - Scope: minimally reuse prefix/suffix and intended-behavior checks; retain paired base/steered on/off-target judgments and add target-blind descriptions with rough magnitudes.
   - Subtle failure mode: persona style substitutes for the intended concept, or target/method/dose metadata tells the blind judge what to find.
   - Discriminator: saved pair examples, full judge requests/responses and numbered outputs expose actual changes and disagreements; blind requests omit target metadata and allow no detectable change.
   - Evidence:
     - Local persona/judge integration: commit `c5c9850`; target-aware AB/BA retained, blind payloads omit intervention metadata and allow no-change descriptions, opaque comparison IDs prevent cross-method/dose merging, blind reports preserve presentation order, and structural persona checks plus an unsent intended-behavior validator request are defined. Final local suite: `70 passed in 7.17s`.
3. [ ] goal: Find useful doses cheaply and test method/model-specific RMS-KL calibration transfer
   - Scope: use iterative search rather than an exhaustive grid; find a useful RMS token-KL target in nats per method/model and test predicted doses on about four new-data cases, including other datasets.
   - Subtle failure mode: near-zero steering passes coherence, reused inputs masquerade as transfer, or a short calibration misses later breakdown.
   - Discriminator: saved search histories and generations compare predicted doses with nearby observed useful/coherent doses on new data, show intended effects and late failures, and distinguish a measured boundary from a search limit; diagnose bugs and iterate within budget.
   - Evidence:
     - Local calibration/transfer orchestration: commit `0f642de`; an observed useful/coherent calibration boundary is measured with real `kl_rms`, stored per method/model with provenance and health, then the existing iterative solver predicts coefficients on four disjoint transfer manifests. Cache reuse/invalidation is tested. Final local suite: `75 passed in 9.05s`; supervisor focused rerun: `5 passed in 1.53s`.
4. [ ] goal: Run a cached Modal `just sweep` within the initial budget
   - Scope: Qwen3.5-4B, 20 numbered development questions; GPU work on Modal, CPU/API judging local; real-pipeline smoke before paid experiments.
   - Subtle failure mode: a rerun pays again, stale outputs survive a meaningful change, or missing billing hides overspending.
   - Discriminator: an unchanged rerun reuses completed work; changed inputs invalidate affected stages; saved manifests, costs and conservative unresolved-cost reservations keep the initial GPU/judge total below $50.
   - Evidence:
     - Non-paid sweep preflight: commit `cc79d9b`; dry planning covers the fixed 20 questions, eight conditions and 50 routed stages without populating production cache. Manifest-derived expected work is `$16.6205564`; one full retry plus quantified unresolved work gives a `$38.1840648` upper bound from sourced Modal/OpenRouter rates. Full offline suite: `78 passed in 7.34s`; supervisor focused rerun: `3 passed in 1.85s`.
     - Production seam and real smoke: commit `e0da829`; a one-question Qwen3.5-4B Modal run completed bare and VJP-cache through train/save-load/attach/generate on full-attention source layer 3 and target layer 4. Recorded `--run` enters the reserving production cache path; maintained tests cover dispatch, reuse, invalidation, identity guards and isolated ledgers. The original `$2` upper reservation remains unresolved, with no judge/API call. Final full suite: `81 passed in 12.53s`; supervisor focused rerun: `3 passed in 6.91s`.
5. [ ] goal: Produce reference-style HTML/PNG Pareto plots and maximum-coherent/optimal-dose tables
   - Scope: preserve the random region and full frontier; report maximum coherent dose separately from the working 1:4 optimum, with links to numbered examples and judge disagreements.
   - Subtle failure mode: attractive plots hide rejected doses, differ from the tables, or imply a general winner from this small comparison.
   - Discriminator: shared measured points feed HTML, PNG and tables; inspect the reference and new PNGs and obtain a cheap independent visual review; explain which methods are powerful/precise here and which results remain uncertain.
   - Evidence:

## UAT / Verification
Open the report, compare the reference/new PNGs, inspect selected and failing numbered response pairs, and rerun `just sweep` from cache; trace plotted/table values to saved judgments, calibration histories and costs.

## Future work / out of scope
The full 100-question evaluation and ~30B/100+B experiments follow the initial interpretable comparison and separate spending approval; retain a scalable Modal entrypoint, but do not claim measured larger-model reliability now. No new concepts, trained steering objectives or unrelated J-lens framework.

```

Use only the statuses that apply. A completed attempt is not necessarily a
completed goal: say what happened. Link evidence where it helps the reader
check a result. End with any action or decision needed from the user.

has forgotten the conversation. Repeat enough context to make each item
clear; prefer "training run" to "run" or "skills repository" to "repo" when
the extra word helps. Be gentle and direct, without praise or persuasion.
Do not invent previous requests or decisions to fill the structure.

We are working together to achieve the user’s goals, not to impress an eval
scorer. Work to understand those goals from the conversation. Avoid grader-folk
language: use the user’s actual terms, not invented metaphors or claims about
how well you performed.

The user is busy and tired, but can still review the work if you explain it
well. Help them understand what happened, why it matters to their goal, and
what needs their judgment. Do not replace that explanation with reassurance
or a checklist of activity.

# Steering-lite BS-bench rewrite

Rewrite the benchmark from vjp-steering on the existing branch. Make a cheap first comparison of steering strength and precision on sycophancy, suitable for use and demo.

## User-visible result
On `rewrite/bsbench-vjp`, a clean cached Modal `just sweep` will compare steering-lite methods, VJP-cache and VJP-diff with prompting/random/mean-difference/PCA controls on 20 numbered Qwen3.5-4B BS-bench v2 questions, validate persona pairs, save on/off-target scores and blind change descriptions, produce matching reference-style HTML/PNG plots and maximum-coherent/optimal-dose tables, and test cheap method/model-specific RMS-KL calibration on about four new-data cases, for less than $50.

## Preferences and authority
- Initial GPU runs and judge calls together cost <$50; use cheaper workers, not Astra. Terra and DeepSeek V4 Flash are approved; keep one implementation writer at a time.
- Preserve the existing judge protocol; add a separate blind call. Dose-selection score: directed intended effect − 4 × off-target effect; retain the full Pareto frontier.
- This is experimental development, not a publication-proof study. No public posting or larger-model spending without separate approval.

## User voice
> can we add VJP-cache and VJP-diff

> yes please. also I wonder if we should uplift steering-lite to match vjp-steering so
>
> - **pairs** I would bring in minimal things in a clean way from  https://github.com/wassname/persona-steering-template-library, namely consider judge validation of the prefix and suffix? and perhaps it can be the same judge and reused from the eval? ok that's the steering personas
>   - but I would also like to use the judge (slow) or activation or J lens to validate if the person pairs correspond to the intended  
> - **calibration** I'm searching for a good way to calibrate so I can find the best dose cheaply and compare pareto optimal or max doses. A grid search is the most expensive. An iteratitive search such as an method of successive approximation (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iterative_method) is faster. But I'v found that (https://github.com/wassname/isokl_steering_calibration). I hope It can find the hyperparameter "target rmse(KL) [nats]" once per method/model, and it will allow quick calibration from then on. I would like to prove this... showing it predict's the max coherent dose on other datasets. (in any case it's better than what other papers and libraries do which is: no think about or talk about this at all, or do a super expensive grid search which I just can't afford).
> - **eval: faithfull** I found using a judge it usefull when the eval is not fully aligned with the steering, the judge can tell use "the effect is bluntness" but we aimed for honesty. another steering method might be more faithful. In fact the eval I used in jvp-steering seems good: it's fairly cheap (100 generations), fairly sensitive, has a nice graph showing the parto, and people understand sycophancy.
> - **platform** run on modal for speed, and still at low cost, and able to scale up from the initial Qwen 3.5 4B model to ~30B or 100+B
>
> so in the end I hope to redo steering-lite with a bullshit bench v2, judged eval, and my nice plot. Hopefully I can have a max dose and optimal dose table too. And compare to prompting as a baseline. Keeping the random zone, and mean mass diff, and PCA baseline.
>
> I migth use the 20 q dev versions first. ofc  the eval needs to be numbered.

>
> which is the best (powerful and precise)?
> is it reliable? does it steer the concept we want fiathfully? does it scale to larger models? and I want a) html plot like vjp-steering (you need to view both png's and compare parity), b) corresponding max dose, and pareto optimal table
>
> the judge must also (this is a bew feature) 1) guess the concept being steered (ideally blind) this will tell us how faithfull it in
>
> need to be clean. we need to be able to run on modal with a `just sweep` where previuslly run ones are cached. we need to use https://github.com/wassname/vjp-steering as a base

> use cheaper models for subagents not astra

## Goals
1. [ ] goal: Rewrite the BS-bench v2 benchmark and compare VJP-cache/VJP-diff with the controls
   - Scope: reuse vjp-steering, preserve steering-lite variants including cache Gram, and include bare, prompting, random, mean difference and PCA; implement cache-value VJPs and reuse VJP-delta as VJP-diff, not a duplicate method.
   - Subtle failure mode: a parallel framework or a nonzero but wrong gradient looks like the requested rewrite.
   - Discriminator: the branch runs the real numbered benchmark; tiny-model extraction, actual cache-value derivatives, attachment, generation and save/load agree with independent checks, including Qwen3.5 hybrid attention.
   - Evidence:
     - Phase-1 cache-value derivatives: commits `2a5ddd3`, `269becf`, `56d10ed`; independent Qwen3.5 hybrid pipeline rerun `48 passed in 46.69s`.
     - Phase-2 local benchmark integration: commit `f26b001`; exact vjp-steering 100-row cohort with fixed numbered first 20, all eight conditions through train/save-load/attach/generate, cache invalidation and ledger tests. Worker full suite: `66 passed in 288.38s`; supervisor focused rerun: `11 passed in 149.83s`.
2. [ ] goal: Validate persona pairs and report judged effects plus blind change descriptions
   - Scope: minimally reuse prefix/suffix and intended-behavior checks; retain paired base/steered on/off-target judgments and add target-blind descriptions with rough magnitudes.
   - Subtle failure mode: persona style substitutes for the intended concept, or target/method/dose metadata tells the blind judge what to find.
   - Discriminator: saved pair examples, full judge requests/responses and numbered outputs expose actual changes and disagreements; blind requests omit target metadata and allow no detectable change.
   - Evidence:
     - Local persona/judge integration: commit `c5c9850`; target-aware AB/BA retained, blind payloads omit intervention metadata and allow no-change descriptions, opaque comparison IDs prevent cross-method/dose merging, blind reports preserve presentation order, and structural persona checks plus an unsent intended-behavior validator request are defined. Final local suite: `70 passed in 7.17s`.
3. [ ] goal: Find useful doses cheaply and test method/model-specific RMS-KL calibration transfer

# busy

> Sorry, I didn't follow and am busy. Can you refresh my memory of where we were and make it easy for me to review what you did toward our goal (gentle intro, refresh my memory, ASD-STE100, goal focused). -- wassname

In wassname's words:

> ok I'm busy, summarise in plain english, context free, focus on action. I want to review what
> you did but forget where we are at, and only have a few minutes

> I am tired and don't have much time, but need to provide some oversight. To help me please
> explain again in ASD-STE100. Please don't assume context and add some redundancy. Please link from the
> goal to your actions and reccomendations. If you need something from me make it clear.

## Required response format

Every `/busy` response uses this structure, including the Markdown checklist.
Do not require the user to also say "sitrep". Render the checklist as Markdown,
not inside a code block.

```md
Our goal is [the user’s goal, with enough context to understand it without
remembering this conversation].

Last time we talked about [topic or decision]. You asked me to [request].

Since then I [brief account of actions, findings, and changes in direction].

## Sitrep

- [x] [Completed goal, action, or attempt, with its result.]
- [/] [Work currently in progress and what remains.]
- [ ] [Future task or unresolved need.]
```

Use only the statuses that apply. A completed attempt is not necessarily a
completed goal: say what happened. Link evidence where it helps the reader
check a result. End with any action or decision needed from the user.

Use plain English (ASD-STE100) and the user’s own terms. Assume the reader
has forgotten the conversation. Repeat enough context to make each item
clear; prefer "training run" to "run" or "skills repository" to "repo" when
the extra word helps. Be gentle and direct, without praise or persuasion.
Do not invent previous requests or decisions to fill the structure.

We are working together to achieve the user’s goals, not to impress an eval
scorer. Work to understand those goals from the conversation. Avoid grader-folk
language: use the user’s actual terms, not invented metaphors or claims about
how well you performed.

The user is busy and tired, but can still review the work if you explain it
well. Help them understand what happened, why it matters to their goal, and
what needs their judgment. Do not replace that explanation with reassurance
or a checklist of activity.

# Quick oracles

Use the `pi-quick-oracles` agent through Nico's `subagent` tool. Consult one oracle at an uncertain branch, or use different model families for independent perspectives. Respect the user's chosen models and budget; discover available models rather than guessing names. Oracles can help during exploration, not only at final review.

## Brief and answer

Write a neutral one-page brief and request about one page back, roughly 500 words each. Include the question, goals, constraints, observations, contrary evidence and known gaps. Attach necessary source excerpts or code separately. Separate observations from interpretation.

Do not lead the witness. Withhold your preferred answer, suspected cause and peer verdicts from initial oracles unless that hypothesis is explicitly the question being examined. Ask each oracle to reconstruct the situation in its own terms. For separate branches, supply the shared facts and each branch's question; keep the first answers independent.

## Clarify and iterate

Check claims against their sources. If there is confusion or missing information, quote the disputed claim, supply the relevant evidence, and request a revised assessment in a new bounded run. If the brief was leading, correct it and test a fresh oracle. Do not coach a desired conclusion.

Repeat until material confusion, leading framing and missing information are resolved. If evidence is unavailable or the agreed budget is exhausted, report what remains unresolved rather than claiming completion. Agreement is not the stopping criterion. Label follow-ups and peer discussion as such, not as independent evidence.

## Budget

Each run shares 4000 generated tokens, including reasoning, across its tool-using turns. At the cutoff, the same child preserves its native conversation, disables tools and gets one final-answer call with minimum supported thinking and a separate 2000-token allowance. A second truncation is incomplete; do not retry it automatically.

`PI_REVIEW_TOKENS` and `PI_ANSWER_TOKENS` can set these allowances before starting Pi; both must be integers of at least 16. Each new run receives a new allowance. Input tokens and external tool costs are not capped.

Load the TypeScript extension only through the child agent, never in the parent session. Unknown APIs and incompatible explicit Anthropic thinking budgets stop with an error. Do not replace native signed/encrypted state with visible text or change backends silently.

-- Pi/OpenAI

```md
# Steering-lite BS-bench rewrite

Rewrite the benchmark from vjp-steering on the existing branch. Make a cheap first comparison of steering strength and precision on sycophancy, suitable for use and demo.

## User-visible result
On `rewrite/bsbench-vjp`, a clean cached Modal `just sweep` will compare steering-lite methods, VJP-cache and VJP-diff with prompting/random/mean-difference/PCA controls on 20 numbered Qwen3.5-4B BS-bench v2 questions, validate persona pairs, save on/off-target scores and blind change descriptions, produce matching reference-style HTML/PNG plots and maximum-coherent/optimal-dose tables, and test cheap method/model-specific RMS-KL calibration on about four new-data cases, for less than $50.

## Preferences and authority
- Initial GPU runs and judge calls together cost <$50; use cheaper workers, not Astra. Terra and DeepSeek V4 Flash are approved; keep one implementation writer at a time.
- Preserve the existing judge protocol; add a separate blind call. Dose-selection score: directed intended effect − 4 × off-target effect; retain the full Pareto frontier.
- This is experimental development, not a publication-proof study. No public posting or larger-model spending without separate approval.

## User voice
> can we add VJP-cache and VJP-diff

> yes please. also I wonder if we should uplift steering-lite to match vjp-steering so
>
> - **pairs** I would bring in minimal things in a clean way from  https://github.com/wassname/persona-steering-template-library, namely consider judge validation of the prefix and suffix? and perhaps it can be the same judge and reused from the eval? ok that's the steering personas
>   - but I would also like to use the judge (slow) or activation or J lens to validate if the person pairs correspond to the intended  
> - **calibration** I'm searching for a good way to calibrate so I can find the best dose cheaply and compare pareto optimal or max doses. A grid search is the most expensive. An iteratitive search such as an method of successive approximation (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iterative_method) is faster. But I'v found that (https://github.com/wassname/isokl_steering_calibration). I hope It can find the hyperparameter "target rmse(KL) [nats]" once per method/model, and it will allow quick calibration from then on. I would like to prove this... showing it predict's the max coherent dose on other datasets. (in any case it's better than what other papers and libraries do which is: no think about or talk about this at all, or do a super expensive grid search which I just can't afford).
> - **eval: faithfull** I found using a judge it usefull when the eval is not fully aligned with the steering, the judge can tell use "the effect is bluntness" but we aimed for honesty. another steering method might be more faithful. In fact the eval I used in jvp-steering seems good: it's fairly cheap (100 generations), fairly sensitive, has a nice graph showing the parto, and people understand sycophancy.
> - **platform** run on modal for speed, and still at low cost, and able to scale up from the initial Qwen 3.5 4B model to ~30B or 100+B
>
> so in the end I hope to redo steering-lite with a bullshit bench v2, judged eval, and my nice plot. Hopefully I can have a max dose and optimal dose table too. And compare to prompting as a baseline. Keeping the random zone, and mean mass diff, and PCA baseline.
>
> I migth use the 20 q dev versions first. ofc  the eval needs to be numbered. 
> In the end I hope to show the best steering method, ansering these questions
>
> which is the best (powerful and precise)?
> is it reliable? does it steer the concept we want fiathfully? does it scale to larger models? and I want a) html plot like vjp-steering (you need to view both png's and compare parity), b) corresponding max dose, and pareto optimal table
>
> the judge must also (this is a bew feature) 1) guess the concept being steered (ideally blind) this will tell us how faithfull it in
>
> need to be clean. we need to be able to run on modal with a `just sweep` where previuslly run ones are cached. we need to use https://github.com/wassname/vjp-steering as a base

> use cheaper models for subagents not astra

## Goals
1. [ ] goal: Rewrite the BS-bench v2 benchmark and compare VJP-cache/VJP-diff with the controls
   - Scope: reuse vjp-steering, preserve steering-lite variants including cache Gram, and include bare, prompting, random, mean difference and PCA; implement cache-value VJPs and reuse VJP-delta as VJP-diff, not a duplicate method.
   - Subtle failure mode: a parallel framework or a nonzero but wrong gradient looks like the requested rewrite.
   - Discriminator: the branch runs the real numbered benchmark; tiny-model extraction, actual cache-value derivatives, attachment, generation and save/load agree with independent checks, including Qwen3.5 hybrid attention.
   - Evidence:
     - Phase-1 cache-value derivatives: commits `2a5ddd3`, `269becf`, `56d10ed`; independent Qwen3.5 hybrid pipeline rerun `48 passed in 46.69s`.
     - Phase-2 local benchmark integration: commit `f26b001`; exact vjp-steering 100-row cohort with fixed numbered first 20, all eight conditions through train/save-load/attach/generate, cache invalidation and ledger tests. Worker full suite: `66 passed in 288.38s`; supervisor focused rerun: `11 passed in 149.83s`.
2. [ ] goal: Validate persona pairs and report judged effects plus blind change descriptions
   - Scope: minimally reuse prefix/suffix and intended-behavior checks; retain paired base/steered on/off-target judgments and add target-blind descriptions with rough magnitudes.
   - Subtle failure mode: persona style substitutes for the intended concept, or target/method/dose metadata tells the blind judge what to find.
   - Discriminator: saved pair examples, full judge requests/responses and numbered outputs expose actual changes and disagreements; blind requests omit target metadata and allow no detectable change.
   - Evidence:
     - Local persona/judge integration: commit `c5c9850`; target-aware AB/BA retained, blind payloads omit intervention metadata and allow no-change descriptions, opaque comparison IDs prevent cross-method/dose merging, blind reports preserve presentation order, and structural persona checks plus an unsent intended-behavior validator request are defined. Final local suite: `70 passed in 7.17s`.
3. [ ] goal: Find useful doses cheaply and test method/model-specific RMS-KL calibration transfer
   - Scope: use iterative search rather than an exhaustive grid; find a useful RMS token-KL target in nats per method/model and test predicted doses on about four new-data cases, including other datasets.
   - Subtle failure mode: near-zero steering passes coherence, reused inputs masquerade as transfer, or a short calibration misses later breakdown.
   - Discriminator: saved search histories and generations compare predicted doses with nearby observed useful/coherent doses on new data, show intended effects and late failures, and distinguish a measured boundary from a search limit; diagnose bugs and iterate within budget.
   - Evidence:
     - Local calibration/transfer orchestration: commit `0f642de`; an observed useful/coherent calibration boundary is measured with real `kl_rms`, stored per method/model with provenance and health, then the existing iterative solver predicts coefficients on four disjoint transfer manifests. Cache reuse/invalidation is tested. Final local suite: `75 passed in 9.05s`; supervisor focused rerun: `5 passed in 1.53s`.
4. [ ] goal: Run a cached Modal `just sweep` within the initial budget
   - Scope: Qwen3.5-4B, 20 numbered development questions; GPU work on Modal, CPU/API judging local; real-pipeline smoke before paid experiments.
   - Subtle failure mode: a rerun pays again, stale outputs survive a meaningful change, or missing billing hides overspending.
   - Discriminator: an unchanged rerun reuses completed work; changed inputs invalidate affected stages; saved manifests, costs and conservative unresolved-cost reservations keep the initial GPU/judge total below $50.
   - Evidence:
     - Non-paid sweep preflight: commit `cc79d9b`; dry planning covers the fixed 20 questions, eight conditions and 50 routed stages without populating production cache. Manifest-derived expected work is `$16.6205564`; one full retry plus quantified unresolved work gives a `$38.1840648` upper bound from sourced Modal/OpenRouter rates. Full offline suite: `78 passed in 7.34s`; supervisor focused rerun: `3 passed in 1.85s`.
     - Production seam and real smoke: commit `e0da829`; a one-question Qwen3.5-4B Modal run completed bare and VJP-cache through train/save-load/attach/generate on full-attention source layer 3 and target layer 4. Recorded `--run` enters the reserving production cache path; maintained tests cover dispatch, reuse, invalidation, identity guards and isolated ledgers. The original `$2` upper reservation remains unresolved, with no judge/API call. Final full suite: `81 passed in 12.53s`; supervisor focused rerun: `3 passed in 6.91s`.
5. [ ] goal: Produce reference-style HTML/PNG Pareto plots and maximum-coherent/optimal-dose tables
   - Scope: preserve the random region and full frontier; report maximum coherent dose separately from the working 1:4 optimum, with links to numbered examples and judge disagreements.
   - Subtle failure mode: attractive plots hide rejected doses, differ from the tables, or imply a general winner from this small comparison.
   - Discriminator: shared measured points feed HTML, PNG and tables; inspect the reference and new PNGs and obtain a cheap independent visual review; explain which methods are powerful/precise here and which results remain uncertain.
   - Evidence:

## UAT / Verification
Open the report, compare the reference/new PNGs, inspect selected and failing numbered response pairs, and rerun `just sweep` from cache; trace plotted/table values to saved judgments, calibration histories and costs.

## Future work / out of scope
The full 100-question evaluation and ~30B/100+B experiments follow the initial interpretable comparison and separate spending approval; retain a scalable Modal entrypoint, but do not claim measured larger-model reliability now. No new concepts, trained steering objectives or unrelated J-lens framework.

# Steering-lite BS-bench rewrite

Rewrite the benchmark from vjp-steering on the existing branch. Make a cheap first comparison of steering strength and precision on sycophancy, suitable for use and demo.

## User-visible result
On `rewrite/bsbench-vjp`, a clean cached Modal `just sweep` will compare steering-lite methods, VJP-cache and VJP-diff with prompting/random/mean-difference/PCA controls on 20 numbered Qwen3.5-4B BS-bench v2 questions, validate persona pairs, save on/off-target scores and blind change descriptions, produce matching reference-style HTML/PNG plots and maximum-coherent/optimal-dose tables, and test cheap method/model-specific RMS-KL calibration on about four new-data cases, for less than $50.

## Preferences and authority
- Initial GPU runs and judge calls together cost <$50; use cheaper workers, not Astra. Terra and DeepSeek V4 Flash are approved; keep one implementation writer at a time.
- Preserve the existing judge protocol; add a separate blind call. Dose-selection score: directed intended effect − 4 × off-target effect; retain the full Pareto frontier.
- This is experimental development, not a publication-proof study. No public posting or larger-model spending without separate approval.

## User voice
> can we add VJP-cache and VJP-diff

> yes please. also I wonder if we should uplift steering-lite to match vjp-steering so
>
> - **pairs** I would bring in minimal things in a clean way from  https://github.com/wassname/persona-steering-template-library, namely consider judge validation of the prefix and suffix? and perhaps it can be the same judge and reused from the eval? ok that's the steering personas
>   - but I would also like to use the judge (slow) or activation or J lens to validate if the person pairs correspond to the intended  
> - **calibration** I'm searching for a good way to calibrate so I can find the best dose cheaply and compare pareto optimal or max doses. A grid search is the most expensive. An iteratitive search such as an method of successive approximation (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iterative_method) is faster. But I'v found that (https://github.com/wassname/isokl_steering_calibration). I hope It can find the hyperparameter "target rmse(KL) [nats]" once per method/model, and it will allow quick calibration from then on. I would like to prove this... showing it predict's the max coherent dose on other datasets. (in any case it's better than what other papers and libraries do which is: no think about or talk about this at all, or do a super expensive grid search which I just can't afford).
> - **eval: faithfull** I found using a judge it usefull when the eval is not fully aligned with the steering, the judge can tell use "the effect is bluntness" but we aimed for honesty. another steering method might be more faithful. In fact the eval I used in jvp-steering seems good: it's fairly cheap (100 generations), fairly sensitive, has a nice graph showing the parto, and people understand sycophancy.
> - **platform** run on modal for speed, and still at low cost, and able to scale up from the initial Qwen 3.5 4B model to ~30B or 100+B
>
> so in the end I hope to redo steering-lite with a bullshit bench v2, judged eval, and my nice plot. Hopefully I can have a max dose and optimal dose table too. And compare to prompting as a baseline. Keeping the random zone, and mean mass diff, and PCA baseline.
>
> I migth use the 20 q dev versions first. ofc  the eval needs to be numbered. 
> In the end I hope to show the best steering method, ansering these questions
>
> which is the best (powerful and precise)?
> is it reliable? does it steer the concept we want fiathfully? does it scale to larger models? and I want a) html plot like vjp-steering (you need to view both png's and compare parity), b) corresponding max dose, and pareto optimal table
>
> the judge must also (this is a bew feature) 1) guess the concept being steered (ideally blind) this will tell us how faithfull it in
>
> need to be clean. we need to be able to run on modal with a `just sweep` where previuslly run ones are cached. we need to use https://github.com/wassname/vjp-steering as a base

> use cheaper models for subagents not astra

## Goals
1. [ ] goal: Rewrite the BS-bench v2 benchmark and compare VJP-cache/VJP-diff with the controls
   - Scope: reuse vjp-steering, preserve steering-lite variants including cache Gram, and include bare, prompting, random, mean difference and PCA; implement cache-value VJPs and reuse VJP-delta as VJP-diff, not a duplicate method.
   - Subtle failure mode: a parallel framework or a nonzero but wrong gradient looks like the requested rewrite.
   - Discriminator: the branch runs the real numbered benchmark; tiny-model extraction, actual cache-value derivatives, attachment, generation and save/load agree with independent checks, including Qwen3.5 hybrid attention.
   - Evidence:
     - Phase-1 cache-value derivatives: commits `2a5ddd3`, `269becf`, `56d10ed`; independent Qwen3.5 hybrid pipeline rerun `48 passed in 46.69s`.
     - Phase-2 local benchmark integration: commit `f26b001`; exact vjp-steering 100-row cohort with fixed numbered first 20, all eight conditions through train/save-load/attach/generate, cache invalidation and ledger tests. Worker full suite: `66 passed in 288.38s`; supervisor focused rerun: `11 passed in 149.83s`.
2. [ ] goal: Validate persona pairs and report judged effects plus blind change descriptions
   - Scope: minimally reuse prefix/suffix and intended-behavior checks; retain paired base/steered on/off-target judgments and add target-blind descriptions with rough magnitudes.
   - Subtle failure mode: persona style substitutes for the intended concept, or target/method/dose metadata tells the blind judge what to find.
   - Discriminator: saved pair examples, full judge requests/responses and numbered outputs expose actual changes and disagreements; blind requests omit target metadata and allow no detectable change.
   - Evidence:
     - Local persona/judge integration: commit `c5c9850`; target-aware AB/BA retained, blind payloads omit intervention metadata and allow no-change descriptions, opaque comparison IDs prevent cross-method/dose merging, blind reports preserve presentation order, and structural persona checks plus an unsent intended-behavior validator request are defined. Final local suite: `70 passed in 7.17s`.
3. [ ] goal: Find useful doses cheaply and test method/model-specific RMS-KL calibration transfer
   - Scope: use iterative search rather than an exhaustive grid; find a useful RMS token-KL target in nats per method/model and test predicted doses on about four new-data cases, including other datasets.
   - Subtle failure mode: near-zero steering passes coherence, reused inputs masquerade as transfer, or a short calibration misses later breakdown.
   - Discriminator: saved search histories and generations compare predicted doses with nearby observed useful/coherent doses on new data, show intended effects and late failures, and distinguish a measured boundary from a search limit; diagnose bugs and iterate within budget.
   - Evidence:
     - Local calibration/transfer orchestration: commit `0f642de`; an observed useful/coherent calibration boundary is measured with real `kl_rms`, stored per method/model with provenance and health, then the existing iterative solver predicts coefficients on four disjoint transfer manifests. Cache reuse/invalidation is tested. Final local suite: `75 passed in 9.05s`; supervisor focused rerun: `5 passed in 1.53s`.
     - Corrected offline transfer contract: commits `2a443f0`, `4c484b8`, `6cc9a6a`; prediction precedes generation at exactly 0.8×/1.0×/1.2× predicted dose, while post-generation classification rejects observations from another case, target or incomplete dose set. Four disjoint cases now load exact provenance-checked records: BS-bench v2 rows 21–24 and the reference project's false-claim agreement prompts. Supervisor reruns: focused `14 passed in 2.91s`; full offline `87 passed in 13.02s`. Real transfer measurements have not run.
4. [ ] goal: Run a cached Modal `just sweep` within the initial budget
   - Scope: Qwen3.5-4B, 20 numbered development questions; GPU work on Modal, CPU/API judging local; real-pipeline smoke before paid experiments.
   - Subtle failure mode: a rerun pays again, stale outputs survive a meaningful change, or missing billing hides overspending.
   - Discriminator: an unchanged rerun reuses completed work; changed inputs invalidate affected stages; saved manifests, costs and conservative unresolved-cost reservations keep the initial GPU/judge total below $50.
   - Evidence:
     - Non-paid sweep preflight: commit `cc79d9b`; dry planning covers the fixed 20 questions, eight conditions and 50 routed stages without populating production cache. Manifest-derived expected work is `$16.6205564`; one full retry plus quantified unresolved work gives a `$38.1840648` upper bound from sourced Modal/OpenRouter rates. Full offline suite: `78 passed in 7.34s`; supervisor focused rerun: `3 passed in 1.85s`.
     - Production seam and real smoke: commit `e0da829`; a one-question Qwen3.5-4B Modal run completed bare and VJP-cache through train/save-load/attach/generate on full-attention source layer 3 and target layer 4. Recorded `--run` enters the reserving production cache path; maintained tests cover dispatch, reuse, invalidation, identity guards and isolated ledgers. The original `$2` upper reservation remains unresolved, with no judge/API call. Final full suite: `81 passed in 12.53s`; supervisor focused rerun: `3 passed in 6.91s`.
     - Corrected non-paid feedback graph and complete-sweep budget: commits `3dc459e`, `eb2b3ab`, `2a443f0`, `4c484b8`, `6cc9a6a`; phase A produces calibration candidates and local judgments before target fitting/prediction, and phase B budgets six vector methods over eight transfer prompts at three doses. The conservative upper bound is `$24.8052168` for 14 GPU stages and 416 aware + 416 blind requests. Transfer records include source revisions and source/content hashes. Supervisor full offline rerun: `87 passed in 13.02s`.
5. [ ] goal: Produce reference-style HTML/PNG Pareto plots and maximum-coherent/optimal-dose tables
   - Scope: preserve the random region and full frontier; report maximum coherent dose separately from the working 1:4 optimum, with links to numbered examples and judge disagreements.
   - Subtle failure mode: attractive plots hide rejected doses, differ from the tables, or imply a general winner from this small comparison.
   - Discriminator: shared measured points feed HTML, PNG and tables; inspect the reference and new PNGs and obtain a cheap independent visual review; explain which methods are powerful/precise here and which results remain uncertain.
   - Evidence:

## UAT / Verification
Open the report, compare the reference/new PNGs, inspect selected and failing numbered response pairs, and rerun `just sweep` from cache; trace plotted/table values to saved judgments, calibration histories and costs.

## Future work / out of scope
The full 100-question evaluation and ~30B/100+B experiments follow the initial interpretable comparison and separate spending approval; retain a scalable Modal entrypoint, but do not claim measured larger-model reliability now. No new concepts, trained steering objectives or unrelated J-lens framework.

# busy

> Sorry, I didn't follow and am busy. Can you refresh my memory of where we were and make it easy for me to review what you did toward our goal (gentle intro, refresh my memory, ASD-STE100, goal focused). -- wassname

In wassname's words:

> ok I'm busy, summarise in plain english, context free, focus on action. I want to review what
> you did but forget where we are at, and only have a few minutes

> I am tired and don't have much time, but need to provide some oversight. To help me please
> explain again in ASD-STE100. Please don't assume context and add some redundancy. Please link from the
> goal to your actions and reccomendations. If you need something from me make it clear.

## Required response format

Every `/busy` response uses this structure, including the Markdown checklist.
Do not require the user to also say "sitrep". Render the checklist as Markdown,
not inside a code block.

```md
Our goal is [the user’s goal, with enough context to understand it without
remembering this conversation].

Last time we talked about [topic or decision]. You asked me to [request].

Since then I [brief account of actions, findings, and changes in direction].

## Sitrep

- [x] [Completed goal, action, or attempt, with its result.]
- [/] [Work currently in progress and what remains.]
- [ ] [Future task or unresolved need.]
```

Use only the statuses that apply. A completed attempt is not necessarily a
completed goal: say what happened. Link evidence where it helps the reader
check a result. End with any action or decision needed from the user.

Use plain English (ASD-STE100) and the user’s own terms. Assume the reader
has forgotten the conversation. Repeat enough context to make each item
clear; prefer "training run" to "run" or "skills repository" to "repo" when
the extra word helps. Be gentle and direct, without praise or persuasion.
Do not invent previous requests or decisions to fill the structure.

We are working together to achieve the user’s goals, not to impress an eval
scorer. Work to understand those goals from the conversation. Avoid grader-folk
language: use the user’s actual terms, not invented metaphors or claims about
how well you performed.

The user is busy and tired, but can still review the work if you explain it
well. Help them understand what happened, why it matters to their goal, and
what needs their judgment. Do not replace that explanation with reassurance
or a checklist of activity.

# Quick oracles

Use the `pi-quick-oracles` agent through Nico's `subagent` tool. Consult one oracle at an uncertain branch, or use different model families for independent perspectives. Respect the user's chosen models and budget; discover available models rather than guessing names. Oracles can help during exploration, not only at final review.

## Brief and answer

Write a neutral one-page brief and request about one page back, roughly 500 words each. Include the question, goals, constraints, observations, contrary evidence and known gaps. Attach necessary source excerpts or code separately. Separate observations from interpretation.

Do not lead the witness. Withhold your preferred answer, suspected cause and peer verdicts from initial oracles unless that hypothesis is explicitly the question being examined. Ask each oracle to reconstruct the situation in its own terms. For separate branches, supply the shared facts and each branch's question; keep the first answers independent.

## Clarify and iterate

Check claims against their sources. If there is confusion or missing information, quote the disputed claim, supply the relevant evidence, and request a revised assessment in a new bounded run. If the brief was leading, correct it and test a fresh oracle. Do not coach a desired conclusion.

Repeat until material confusion, leading framing and missing information are resolved. If evidence is unavailable or the agreed budget is exhausted, report what remains unresolved rather than claiming completion. Agreement is not the stopping criterion. Label follow-ups and peer discussion as such, not as independent evidence.

## Budget

Each run shares 4000 generated tokens, including reasoning, across its tool-using turns. At the cutoff, the same child preserves its native conversation, disables tools and gets one final-answer call with minimum supported thinking and a separate 2000-token allowance. A second truncation is incomplete; do not retry it automatically.

`PI_REVIEW_TOKENS` and `PI_ANSWER_TOKENS` can set these allowances before starting Pi; both must be integers of at least 16. Each new run receives a new allowance. Input tokens and external tool costs are not capped.

Load the TypeScript extension only through the child agent, never in the parent session. Unknown APIs and incompatible explicit Anthropic thinking budgets stop with an error. Do not replace native signed/encrypted state with visible text or change backends silently.

-- Pi/OpenAI

```md
# Steering-lite BS-bench rewrite

Rewrite the benchmark from vjp-steering on the existing branch. Make a cheap first comparison of steering strength and precision on sycophancy, suitable for use and demo.

## User-visible result
On `rewrite/bsbench-vjp`, a clean cached Modal `just sweep` will compare steering-lite methods, VJP-cache and VJP-diff with prompting/random/mean-difference/PCA controls on 20 numbered Qwen3.5-4B BS-bench v2 questions, validate persona pairs, save on/off-target scores and blind change descriptions, produce matching reference-style HTML/PNG plots and maximum-coherent/optimal-dose tables, and test cheap method/model-specific RMS-KL calibration on about four new-data cases, for less than $50.

## Preferences and authority
- Initial GPU runs and judge calls together cost <$50; use cheaper workers, not Astra. Terra and DeepSeek V4 Flash are approved; keep one implementation writer at a time.
- Preserve the existing judge protocol; add a separate blind call. Dose-selection score: directed intended effect − 4 × off-target effect; retain the full Pareto frontier.
- This is experimental development, not a publication-proof study. No public posting or larger-model spending without separate approval.

## User voice
> can we add VJP-cache and VJP-diff

> yes please. also I wonder if we should uplift steering-lite to match vjp-steering so
>
> - **pairs** I would bring in minimal things in a clean way from  https://github.com/wassname/persona-steering-template-library, namely consider judge validation of the prefix and suffix? and perhaps it can be the same judge and reused from the eval? ok that's the steering personas
>   - but I would also like to use the judge (slow) or activation or J lens to validate if the person pairs correspond to the intended  
> - **calibration** I'm searching for a good way to calibrate so I can find the best dose cheaply and compare pareto optimal or max doses. A grid search is the most expensive. An iteratitive search such as an method of successive approximation (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iterative_method) is faster. But I'v found that (https://github.com/wassname/isokl_steering_calibration). I hope It can find the hyperparameter "target rmse(KL) [nats]" once per method/model, and it will allow quick calibration from then on. I would like to prove this... showing it predict's the max coherent dose on other datasets. (in any case it's better than what other papers and libraries do which is: no think about or talk about this at all, or do a super expensive grid search which I just can't afford).
> - **eval: faithfull** I found using a judge it usefull when the eval is not fully aligned with the steering, the judge can tell use "the effect is bluntness" but we aimed for honesty. another steering method might be more faithful. In fact the eval I used in jvp-steering seems good: it's fairly cheap (100 generations), fairly sensitive, has a nice graph showing the parto, and people understand sycophancy.
> - **platform** run on modal for speed, and still at low cost, and able to scale up from the initial Qwen 3.5 4B model to ~30B or 100+B
>
> so in the end I hope to redo steering-lite with a bullshit bench v2, judged eval, and my nice plot. Hopefully I can have a max dose and optimal dose table too. And compare to prompting as a baseline. Keeping the random zone, and mean mass diff, and PCA baseline.
>
> I migth use the 20 q dev versions first. ofc  the eval needs to be numbered. 
> In the end I hope to show the best steering method, ansering these questions
>
> which is the best (powerful and precise)?
> is it reliable? does it steer the concept we want fiathfully? does it scale to larger models? and I want a) html plot like vjp-steering (you need to view both png's and compare parity), b) corresponding max dose, and pareto optimal table
>
> the judge must also (this is a bew feature) 1) guess the concept being steered (ideally blind) this will tell us how faithfull it in
>
> need to be clean. we need to be able to run on modal with a `just sweep` where previuslly run ones are cached. we need to use https://github.com/wassname/vjp-steering as a base

> use cheaper models for subagents not astra

## Goals
1. [ ] goal: Rewrite the BS-bench v2 benchmark and compare VJP-cache/VJP-diff with the controls
   - Scope: reuse vjp-steering, preserve steering-lite variants including cache Gram, and include bare, prompting, random, mean difference and PCA; implement cache-value VJPs and reuse VJP-delta as VJP-diff, not a duplicate method.
   - Subtle failure mode: a parallel framework or a nonzero but wrong gradient looks like the requested rewrite.
   - Discriminator: the branch runs the real numbered benchmark; tiny-model extraction, actual cache-value derivatives, attachment, generation and save/load agree with independent checks, including Qwen3.5 hybrid attention.
   - Evidence:
     - Phase-1 cache-value derivatives: commits `2a5ddd3`, `269becf`, `56d10ed`; independent Qwen3.5 hybrid pipeline rerun `48 passed in 46.69s`.
     - Phase-2 local benchmark integration: commit `f26b001`; exact vjp-steering 100-row cohort with fixed numbered first 20, all eight conditions through train/save-load/attach/generate, cache invalidation and ledger tests. Worker full suite: `66 passed in 288.38s`; supervisor focused rerun: `11 passed in 149.83s`.
2. [ ] goal: Validate persona pairs and report judged effects plus blind change descriptions
   - Scope: minimally reuse prefix/suffix and intended-behavior checks; retain paired base/steered on/off-target judgments and add target-blind descriptions with rough magnitudes.
   - Subtle failure mode: persona style substitutes for the intended concept, or target/method/dose metadata tells the blind judge what to find.
   - Discriminator: saved pair examples, full judge requests/responses and numbered outputs expose actual changes and disagreements; blind requests omit target metadata and allow no detectable change.
   - Evidence:
     - Local persona/judge integration: commit `c5c9850`; target-aware AB/BA retained, blind payloads omit intervention metadata and allow no-change descriptions, opaque comparison IDs prevent cross-method/dose merging, blind reports preserve presentation order, and structural persona checks plus an unsent intended-behavior validator request are defined. Final local suite: `70 passed in 7.17s`.
3. [ ] goal: Find useful doses cheaply and test method/model-specific RMS-KL calibration transfer
   - Scope: use iterative search rather than an exhaustive grid; find a useful RMS token-KL target in nats per method/model and test predicted doses on about four new-data cases, including other datasets.
   - Subtle failure mode: near-zero steering passes coherence, reused inputs masquerade as transfer, or a short calibration misses later breakdown.
   - Discriminator: saved search histories and generations compare predicted doses with nearby observed useful/coherent doses on new data, show intended effects and late failures, and distinguish a measured boundary from a search limit; diagnose bugs and iterate within budget.
   - Evidence:
     - Local calibration/transfer orchestration: commit `0f642de`; an observed useful/coherent calibration boundary is measured with real `kl_rms`, stored per method/model with provenance and health, then the existing iterative solver predicts coefficients on four disjoint transfer manifests. Cache reuse/invalidation is tested. Final local suite: `75 passed in 9.05s`; supervisor focused rerun: `5 passed in 1.53s`.
4. [ ] goal: Run a cached Modal `just sweep` within the initial budget
   - Scope: Qwen3.5-4B, 20 numbered development questions; GPU work on Modal, CPU/API judging local; real-pipeline smoke before paid experiments.
   - Subtle failure mode: a rerun pays again, stale outputs survive a meaningful change, or missing billing hides overspending.
   - Discriminator: an unchanged rerun reuses completed work; changed inputs invalidate affected stages; saved manifests, costs and conservative unresolved-cost reservations keep the initial GPU/judge total below $50.
   - Evidence:
     - Non-paid sweep preflight: commit `cc79d9b`; dry planning covers the fixed 20 questions, eight conditions and 50 routed stages without populating production cache. Manifest-derived expected work is `$16.6205564`; one full retry plus quantified unresolved work gives a `$38.1840648` upper bound from sourced Modal/OpenRouter rates. Full offline suite: `78 passed in 7.34s`; supervisor focused rerun: `3 passed in 1.85s`.
     - Production seam and real smoke: commit `e0da829`; a one-question Qwen3.5-4B Modal run completed bare and VJP-cache through train/save-load/attach/generate on full-attention source layer 3 and target layer 4. Recorded `--run` enters the reserving production cache path; maintained tests cover dispatch, reuse, invalidation, identity guards and isolated ledgers. The original `$2` upper reservation remains unresolved, with no judge/API call. Final full suite: `81 passed in 12.53s`; supervisor focused rerun: `3 passed in 6.91s`.
5. [ ] goal: Produce reference-style HTML/PNG Pareto plots and maximum-coherent/optimal-dose tables
   - Scope: preserve the random region and full frontier; report maximum coherent dose separately from the working 1:4 optimum, with links to numbered examples and judge disagreements.
   - Subtle failure mode: attractive plots hide rejected doses, differ from the tables, or imply a general winner from this small comparison.
   - Discriminator: shared measured points feed HTML, PNG and tables; inspect the reference and new PNGs and obtain a cheap independent visual review; explain which methods are powerful/precise here and which results remain uncertain.
   - Evidence:

## UAT / Verification
Open the report, compare the reference/new PNGs, inspect selected and failing numbered response pairs, and rerun `just sweep` from cache; trace plotted/table values to saved judgments, calibration histories and costs.

## Future work / out of scope
The full 100-question evaluation and ~30B/100+B experiments follow the initial interpretable comparison and separate spending approval; retain a scalable Modal entrypoint, but do not claim measured larger-model reliability now. No new concepts, trained steering objectives or unrelated J-lens framework.

reviewer:
## Review: commit 9ebb92c (bounded fake/live orchestration slice)

### Observations

**`upper_usd=0.01` hard-coded (production.py: `run_direct_condition`, `run_live_two_step` calibration_config, final_config).** The dry accounting in `sweep.py` assumes `GPU_HOURS_PER_STAGE=0.5` at $1.10/GPU-hour plus CPU/memory — ≈$0.60 per GPU stage. So each real Modal stage would be dispatched against a reservation ~55× too small. Consequences, confirmed in `cache.py`:
- `settle()` raises only *after* writing the settled record and after money is spent ("actual cost exceeded reservation"), and since `cached_stage`'s compute raised, the completed GPU result is **not cached** — a retry re-dispatches and pays again.
- The $50 reserve-time guard is bypassed per stage: 14 real stages could commit ~$8 while the ledger shows $0.14 reserved.

This does **not** block accepting the bounded fake slice (fake `actual_usd=0.0`, and no paid path is reachable via `--backend fake`), but it is a **hard pre-paid gate**: the value lives in `production.py`, the very module the paid backend will reuse, so it will ship silently into paid dispatch unless fixed first.

**`CANDIDATE_DOSE_UPPER=12` attribution is wrong (sweep.py:26).** The comment ties it to `calibrate_iso_kl(max_iters=12)`, but (a) phase-A candidate doses are backend-produced behavioral generations, not solver iterations, and (b) `calibrate_iso_kl` itself is not bounded by `max_iters`: the initial bracket/halving loop (`calibrate.py:~495-510`, up to ~18 evals for the (0.001,256) bracket), 12 Illinois iterations, `sign_probe` (2 evals), and `_finalize` all add measurements beyond 12. The fail-fast guard in `production.py` makes the direction safe (rejects >12 before settlement), but if the real backend reuses that solver for candidate generation, legitimate runs will die after the candidate GPU stage is paid for and uncached. Separately, the dry-manifest item_count change (4×12=48) inflates judge estimates 416→944 — conservative, fine.

**Non-blocking concerns:**
- `final_config` embeds `vector_artifact.backend_path` as an absolute resolved path; the final-generation cache identity is therefore machine/root-dependent and the recorded manifest is not portable.
- Failed validation leaves the reservation open in the ledger (never settled). Conservative and acceptable, but worth documenting.
- `run_direct_condition`/`run_live_two_step` local-stage identities include the time-based `reservation` id; stable across cache hits, but it makes identities opaque to audit — mild.

**Verified good:** fail-fast ordering (validation before `settle`, tested), durable sidecar re-verified on cache hit before final dispatch, exact candidate coverage checks, invalidation tests for judgments/provenance/persona identity, real `fit_target`/`predict_transfer` wired with injected measure/solver.

### Blocking defects
None for the fake slice. For paid enablement: the `upper_usd=0.01` under-reservation is blocking.

### Verdict
Accept this bounded fake/local slice. It does not complete goal 4 and must not enable the paid backend until the reservation uppers match the dry-manifest per-stage accounting.

### Smallest next step
Replace the three hard-coded `upper_usd: 0.01` values in `production.py` with a shared per-stage upper derived from `sweep.py`'s own constants (0.5 GPU-hour × rates + CPU/memory), and add one test asserting reservation uppers equal the dry-manifest per-stage assumption; also reconcile `CANDIDATE_DOSE_UPPER` with the actual backend candidate-search bound (bracket + iterations + finalize) rather than `max_iters`.

# Steering-lite BS-bench rewrite

Rewrite the benchmark from vjp-steering on the existing branch. Make a cheap first comparison of steering strength and precision on sycophancy, suitable for use and demo.

## User-visible result
On `rewrite/bsbench-vjp`, a clean cached Modal `just sweep` will compare steering-lite methods, VJP-cache and VJP-diff with prompting/random/mean-difference/PCA controls on 20 numbered Qwen3.5-4B BS-bench v2 questions, validate persona pairs, save on/off-target scores and blind change descriptions, produce matching reference-style HTML/PNG plots and maximum-coherent/optimal-dose tables, and test cheap method/model-specific RMS-KL calibration on about four new-data cases, for less than $50.

## Preferences and authority
- Initial GPU runs and judge calls together cost <$50; use cheaper workers, not Astra. Terra and DeepSeek V4 Flash are approved; keep one implementation writer at a time.
- Preserve the existing judge protocol; add a separate blind call. Dose-selection score: directed intended effect − 4 × off-target effect; retain the full Pareto frontier.
- This is experimental development, not a publication-proof study. No public posting or larger-model spending without separate approval.

## User voice
> can we add VJP-cache and VJP-diff

> yes please. also I wonder if we should uplift steering-lite to match vjp-steering so
>
> - **pairs** I would bring in minimal things in a clean way from  https://github.com/wassname/persona-steering-template-library, namely consider judge validation of the prefix and suffix? and perhaps it can be the same judge and reused from the eval? ok that's the steering personas
>   - but I would also like to use the judge (slow) or activation or J lens to validate if the person pairs correspond to the intended  
> - **calibration** I'm searching for a good way to calibrate so I can find the best dose cheaply and compare pareto optimal or max doses. A grid search is the most expensive. An iteratitive search such as an method of successive approximation (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iterative_method) is faster. But I'v found that (https://github.com/wassname/isokl_steering_calibration). I hope It can find the hyperparameter "target rmse(KL) [nats]" once per method/model, and it will allow quick calibration from then on. I would like to prove this... showing it predict's the max coherent dose on other datasets. (in any case it's better than what other papers and libraries do which is: no think about or talk about this at all, or do a super expensive grid search which I just can't afford).
> - **eval: faithfull** I found using a judge it usefull when the eval is not fully aligned with the steering, the judge can tell use "the effect is bluntness" but we aimed for honesty. another steering method might be more faithful. In fact the eval I used in jvp-steering seems good: it's fairly cheap (100 generations), fairly sensitive, has a nice graph showing the parto, and people understand sycophancy.
> - **platform** run on modal for speed, and still at low cost, and able to scale up from the initial Qwen 3.5 4B model to ~30B or 100+B
>
> so in the end I hope to redo steering-lite with a bullshit bench v2, judged eval, and my nice plot. Hopefully I can have a max dose and optimal dose table too. And compare to prompting as a baseline. Keeping the random zone, and mean mass diff, and PCA baseline.
>
> I migth use the 20 q dev versions first. ofc  the eval needs to be numbered. 
> In the end I hope to show the best steering method, ansering these questions
>
> which is the best (powerful and precise)?
> is it reliable? does it steer the concept we want fiathfully? does it scale to larger models? and I want a) html plot like vjp-steering (you need to view both png's and compare parity), b) corresponding max dose, and pareto optimal table
>
> the judge must also (this is a bew feature) 1) guess the concept being steered (ideally blind) this will tell us how faithfull it in
>
> need to be clean. we need to be able to run on modal with a `just sweep` where previuslly run ones are cached. we need to use https://github.com/wassname/vjp-steering as a base

> use cheaper models for subagents not astra

## Goals
1. [ ] goal: Rewrite the BS-bench v2 benchmark and compare VJP-cache/VJP-diff with the controls
   - Scope: reuse vjp-steering, preserve steering-lite variants including cache Gram, and include bare, prompting, random, mean difference and PCA; implement cache-value VJPs and reuse VJP-delta as VJP-diff, not a duplicate method.
   - Subtle failure mode: a parallel framework or a nonzero but wrong gradient looks like the requested rewrite.
   - Discriminator: the branch runs the real numbered benchmark; tiny-model extraction, actual cache-value derivatives, attachment, generation and save/load agree with independent checks, including Qwen3.5 hybrid attention.
   - Evidence:
     - Phase-1 cache-value derivatives: commits `2a5ddd3`, `269becf`, `56d10ed`; independent Qwen3.5 hybrid pipeline rerun `48 passed in 46.69s`.
     - Phase-2 local benchmark integration: commit `f26b001`; exact vjp-steering 100-row cohort with fixed numbered first 20, all eight conditions through train/save-load/attach/generate, cache invalidation and ledger tests. Worker full suite: `66 passed in 288.38s`; supervisor focused rerun: `11 passed in 149.83s`.
2. [ ] goal: Validate persona pairs and report judged effects plus blind change descriptions
   - Scope: minimally reuse prefix/suffix and intended-behavior checks; retain paired base/steered on/off-target judgments and add target-blind descriptions with rough magnitudes.
   - Subtle failure mode: persona style substitutes for the intended concept, or target/method/dose metadata tells the blind judge what to find.
   - Discriminator: saved pair examples, full judge requests/responses and numbered outputs expose actual changes and disagreements; blind requests omit target metadata and allow no detectable change.
   - Evidence:
     - Local persona/judge integration: commit `c5c9850`; target-aware AB/BA retained, blind payloads omit intervention metadata and allow no-change descriptions, opaque comparison IDs prevent cross-method/dose merging, blind reports preserve presentation order, and structural persona checks plus an unsent intended-behavior validator request are defined. Final local suite: `70 passed in 7.17s`.
3. [ ] goal: Find useful doses cheaply and test method/model-specific RMS-KL calibration transfer
   - Scope: use iterative search rather than an exhaustive grid; find a useful RMS token-KL target in nats per method/model and test predicted doses on about four new-data cases, including other datasets.
   - Subtle failure mode: near-zero steering passes coherence, reused inputs masquerade as transfer, or a short calibration misses later breakdown.
   - Discriminator: saved search histories and generations compare predicted doses with nearby observed useful/coherent doses on new data, show intended effects and late failures, and distinguish a measured boundary from a search limit; diagnose bugs and iterate within budget.
   - Evidence:
     - Local calibration/transfer orchestration: commit `0f642de`; an observed useful/coherent calibration boundary is measured with real `kl_rms`, stored per method/model with provenance and health, then the existing iterative solver predicts coefficients on four disjoint transfer manifests. Cache reuse/invalidation is tested. Final local suite: `75 passed in 9.05s`; supervisor focused rerun: `5 passed in 1.53s`.
     - Corrected offline transfer contract: commits `2a443f0`, `4c484b8`, `6cc9a6a`; prediction precedes generation at exactly 0.8×/1.0×/1.2× predicted dose, while post-generation classification rejects observations from another case, target or incomplete dose set. Four disjoint cases now load exact provenance-checked records: BS-bench v2 rows 21–24 and the reference project's false-claim agreement prompts. Supervisor reruns: focused `14 passed in 2.91s`; full offline `87 passed in 13.02s`. Real transfer measurements have not run.
4. [ ] goal: Run a cached Modal `just sweep` within the initial budget
   - Scope: Qwen3.5-4B, 20 numbered development questions; GPU work on Modal, CPU/API judging local; real-pipeline smoke before paid experiments.
   - Subtle failure mode: a rerun pays again, stale outputs survive a meaningful change, or missing billing hides overspending.
   - Discriminator: an unchanged rerun reuses completed work; changed inputs invalidate affected stages; saved manifests, costs and conservative unresolved-cost reservations keep the initial GPU/judge total below $50.
   - Evidence:
     - Non-paid sweep preflight: commit `cc79d9b`; dry planning covers the fixed 20 questions, eight conditions and 50 routed stages without populating production cache. Manifest-derived expected work is `$16.6205564`; one full retry plus quantified unresolved work gives a `$38.1840648` upper bound from sourced Modal/OpenRouter rates. Full offline suite: `78 passed in 7.34s`; supervisor focused rerun: `3 passed in 1.85s`.
     - Production seam and real smoke: commit `e0da829`; a one-question Qwen3.5-4B Modal run completed bare and VJP-cache through train/save-load/attach/generate on full-attention source layer 3 and target layer 4. Recorded `--run` enters the reserving production cache path; maintained tests cover dispatch, reuse, invalidation, identity guards and isolated ledgers. The original `$2` upper reservation remains unresolved, with no judge/API call. Final full suite: `81 passed in 12.53s`; supervisor focused rerun: `3 passed in 6.91s`.
     - Corrected non-paid feedback graph and complete-sweep budget: commits `3dc459e`, `eb2b3ab`, `2a443f0`, `4c484b8`, `6cc9a6a`; phase A produces calibration candidates and local judgments before target fitting/prediction, and phase B budgets six vector methods over eight transfer prompts at three doses. The conservative upper bound is `$24.8052168` for 14 GPU stages and 416 aware + 416 blind requests. Transfer records include source revisions and source/content hashes. Supervisor full offline rerun: `87 passed in 13.02s`.
5. [ ] goal: Produce reference-style HTML/PNG Pareto plots and maximum-coherent/optimal-dose tables
   - Scope: preserve the random region and full frontier; report maximum coherent dose separately from the working 1:4 optimum, with links to numbered examples and judge disagreements.
   - Subtle failure mode: attractive plots hide rejected doses, differ from the tables, or imply a general winner from this small comparison.
   - Discriminator: shared measured points feed HTML, PNG and tables; inspect the reference and new PNGs and obtain a cheap independent visual review; explain which methods are powerful/precise here and which results remain uncertain.
   - Evidence:

## UAT / Verification
Open the report, compare the reference/new PNGs, inspect selected and failing numbered response pairs, and rerun `just sweep` from cache; trace plotted/table values to saved judgments, calibration histories and costs.

## Future work / out of scope
The full 100-question evaluation and ~30B/100+B experiments follow the initial interpretable comparison and separate spending approval; retain a scalable Modal entrypoint, but do not claim measured larger-model reliability now. No new concepts, trained steering objectives or unrelated J-lens framework.

# Steering-lite BS-bench rewrite

Rewrite the benchmark from vjp-steering on the existing branch. Make a cheap first comparison of steering strength and precision on sycophancy, suitable for use and demo.

## User-visible result
On `rewrite/bsbench-vjp`, a clean cached Modal `just sweep` will compare steering-lite methods, VJP-cache and VJP-diff with prompting/random/mean-difference/PCA controls on 20 numbered Qwen3.5-4B BS-bench v2 questions, validate persona pairs, save on/off-target scores and blind change descriptions, produce matching reference-style HTML/PNG plots and maximum-coherent/optimal-dose tables, and test cheap method/model-specific RMS-KL calibration on about four new-data cases, for less than $50.

## Preferences and authority
- Initial GPU runs and judge calls together cost <$50; use cheaper workers, not Astra. Terra and DeepSeek V4 Flash are approved; keep one implementation writer at a time.
- Preserve the existing judge protocol; add a separate blind call. Dose-selection score: directed intended effect − 4 × off-target effect; retain the full Pareto frontier.
- This is experimental development, not a publication-proof study. No public posting or larger-model spending without separate approval.

## User voice
> can we add VJP-cache and VJP-diff

> yes please. also I wonder if we should uplift steering-lite to match vjp-steering so
>
> - **pairs** I would bring in minimal things in a clean way from  https://github.com/wassname/persona-steering-template-library, namely consider judge validation of the prefix and suffix? and perhaps it can be the same judge and reused from the eval? ok that's the steering personas
>   - but I would also like to use the judge (slow) or activation or J lens to validate if the person pairs correspond to the intended  
> - **calibration** I'm searching for a good way to calibrate so I can find the best dose cheaply and compare pareto optimal or max doses. A grid search is the most expensive. An iteratitive search such as an method of successive approximation (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iterative_method) is faster. But I'v found that (https://github.com/wassname/isokl_steering_calibration). I hope It can find the hyperparameter "target rmse(KL) [nats]" once per method/model, and it will allow quick calibration from then on. I would like to prove this... showing it predict's the max coherent dose on other datasets. (in any case it's better than what other papers and libraries do which is: no think about or talk about this at all, or do a super expensive grid search which I just can't afford).
> - **eval: faithfull** I found using a judge it usefull when the eval is not fully aligned with the steering, the judge can tell use "the effect is bluntness" but we aimed for honesty. another steering method might be more faithful. In fact the eval I used in jvp-steering seems good: it's fairly cheap (100 generations), fairly sensitive, has a nice graph showing the parto, and people understand sycophancy.
> - **platform** run on modal for speed, and still at low cost, and able to scale up from the initial Qwen 3.5 4B model to ~30B or 100+B
>
> so in the end I hope to redo steering-lite with a bullshit bench v2, judged eval, and my nice plot. Hopefully I can have a max dose and optimal dose table too. And compare to prompting as a baseline. Keeping the random zone, and mean mass diff, and PCA baseline.
>
> I migth use the 20 q dev versions first. ofc  the eval needs to be numbered. 
> In the end I hope to show the best steering method, ansering these questions
>
> which is the best (powerful and precise)?
> is it reliable? does it steer the concept we want fiathfully? does it scale to larger models? and I want a) html plot like vjp-steering (you need to view both png's and compare parity), b) corresponding max dose, and pareto optimal table
>
> the judge must also (this is a bew feature) 1) guess the concept being steered (ideally blind) this will tell us how faithfull it in
>
> need to be clean. we need to be able to run on modal with a `just sweep` where previuslly run ones are cached. we need to use https://github.com/wassname/vjp-steering as a base

> use cheaper models for subagents not astra

## Goals

   - Scope: reuse vjp-steering, preserve steering-lite variants including cache Gram, and include bare, prompting, random, mean difference and PCA; implement cache-value VJPs and reuse VJP-delta as VJP-diff, not a duplicate method.
   - Subtle failure mode: a parallel framework or a nonzero but wrong gradient looks like the requested rewrite.

Worker full suite: `66 passed in 288.38s`; supervisor focused rerun: `11 passed in 149.83s`.

   - Scope: minimally reuse prefix/suffix and intended-behavior checks; retain paired base/steered on/off-target judgments and add target-blind descriptions with rough magnitudes.

   - Subtle failure mode: a rerun pays again, stale outputs survive a meaningful change, or missing billing hides overspending.

   - Evidence:
